$comment: Executable receipts for the numbers dsh-xray publishes in prose. Every claim carries a `check`: either a command that recomputes the figure from committed data (fixtures/, bin/, lib/, tests/) or `check.manual` with the reason no command can. Run with `python3 -m verify_claims --root . run`; CI runs it via .github/workflows/claims.yml.

claims.claim: The CLI dispatches ten commands — attribute, conflicts, diff, snapshot, deps, health, cost, shadow, verify, audit.
claims.metric: entries in the `commands` dispatch table of bin/xray.js
claims.method: The table maps ten names to their cmd* functions, and the same ten appear in the README's CLI block and in the CLI's own usage banner. `deps`, `health`, `cost`, `shadow` and `verify` need the plugin mounted (they read the runtime snapshot); the other five run statically.

claims.claim: The CLI's live-panel hint prints `http://127.0.0.1:3080/xray` (the web app's default bind), not `localhost`.
claims.metric: the panel URL printed by the CLI's runtime commands
claims.method: `deps` ends with panelHint(), which prints the hint unless --json is set. The check copies the committed fixtures/runtime-basic snapshot into a throwaway $DSH_HOME so the command really runs, then reads the hint line. The 2026-09-12 correction recorded in CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased entry replaced `localhost:3080` with this address in the READMEs and in the CLI hint; the upstream half of the statement is `panel-default-bind`.
claims.repro: D=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir -p $D/xray && cp fixtures/runtime-basic/runtime.json $D/xray/runtime.json && DSH_HOME=$D node bin/xray.js deps | grep '^live panel:'

check.cmd: D=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir -p $D/xray && cp fixtures/runtime-basic/runtime.json $D/xray/runtime.json && DSH_HOME=$D node bin/xray.js deps | grep '^live panel:'

claims.claim: 3080 on 127.0.0.1 is the DeepSeek Harness web app's default bind, not a choice of dsh-xray.
claims.metric: host/port defaults in the upstream web-app bundle patch
claims.method: Upstream packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml sets `host: !!js ctx.webStartup.host ?? '127.0.0.1'` and `port: !!js ctx.webStartup.port ?? 3080`. The 2026-09-12 docs correction (recorded in CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased entry) changed the READMEs and the CLI hint to this address on that source.

check.manual: The default bind lives in the upstream deepseek-harness web-app bundle, not in this repository: no committed file here carries the host/port defaults, and reading them needs network access to upstream, which the checks must not require. Corroborated on this machine by the installed bundle (~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app/cordis.patch.yml). The half the repository can recompute — that its own CLI prints exactly this address — is checked by `panel-hint-address`.

claims.claim: The committed runtime fixture `fixtures/runtime-basic` pins the disable-cascade row `ToolRuntime → 1 plugin(s): AgentLoop`.
claims.metric: cascade rows the committed runtime fixture yields through the real serviceGraph()
claims.method: fixtures/runtime-basic/runtime.json is the repo's committed runtime snapshot; both READMEs cite its pinned output as the synthetic contrast to the illustrative `Loader → 5` capture. The check re-derives the row with lib/model.js serviceGraph() instead of reading the pinned line.

claims.claim: The README hero waterfall figures — system 500, tool schemas 420, history 200, tool results 80, about 1200 in total — are the request ledger of the committed `fixtures/runtime-basic` snapshot.
claims.metric: the per-request ledger cells of the committed fixture's pinned requests view
claims.method: The hero caption states the token-ledger panel is measured on the committed fixtures/runtime-basic snapshot, and hero.svg's <desc> lists the same four cells plus the total. expected.json is the pinned output that tests/golden.spec.js reproduces; the check prints the four cells and the total from it.

claims.claim: Context token counts are estimates at roughly 4 chars per token.
claims.metric: chars per estimated token in lib/collect/runtime.js estimateTokens()
claims.method: The README's Analysis-modes table says token counts are estimates (~4 chars/token) unless the entry text is opened and counted, and the entry payload reports the estimator as `~4 chars/token`. The check feeds 400 characters to the real estimator and prints its token count plus the implied chars-per-token.

claims.claim: The suite is 62 unit tests plus 8 end-to-end tests that drive a real dsh install and skip cleanly when none is present.
claims.metric: tests reported by the runner for the unit specs (the e2e file needs a live dsh)
claims.method: node --test over every spec except e2e.spec.js; the runner's own TAP summary is asserted

check.cmd: node --test $(ls tests/*.spec.js | grep -v e2e.spec.js) 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^# \(tests\|pass\|fail\) /\1=/p' | tr '\n' ' '

claims.claim: The README's `deps` sample (`Loader → 5 plugin(s): AgentPresets, ClientModuleRegistry, Hmr, …` / `TimerService → 1 plugin(s): Hmr`) is an illustrative capture of an author profile, not a reproducible figure.
claims.metric: cascade row counts as printed in the sample block
claims.method: The block carries its own provenance note, and neither AgentPresets nor TimerService appears in any committed fixture. The sample is published in both READMEs' feature tables and in the hero's disable-cascade panel.

check.manual: No committed fixture reproduces these counts, and the README labels the block as illustrative: "Illustrative capture from the author's `web` profile (revision unrecorded) — no committed fixture produces it, and the counts drift as plugins are added; this repo's runtime fixtures are synthetic (e.g. `fixtures/runtime-basic` pins `ToolRuntime → 1 plugin(s): AgentLoop`)." The hero caption repeats it: "the disable-cascade panel is an illustrative capture from an author profile that no committed fixture reproduces". `grep -rIl -E 'AgentPresets|TimerService' fixtures lib bin tests` finds nothing, so there is no input to feed a check. The reproducible counterpart of this panel is `runtime-fixture-cascade`.

claims.claim: The demo transcript's cost figures — `~1625 tokens: 1 tool schema(s) ~121 + 19 prompt section(s) ~1504`, `app:web-surface ~248`, `tool:goal ~184` — are an illustrative capture, not reproducible from this repository.
claims.metric: the cost view's totals and per-row estimates in the published transcript
claims.method: The transcript is docs/demo.svg, reproduced in docs/discussion-post-draft.md; both READMEs caption it and the SVG carries a <desc> saying the figures are not reproducible from the synthetic fixtures. The same capture's `hmr ← patched by dsh-web-app [disabled]` row is real for the @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app 0.1.0-rc.6 line but records no harness revision.

check.manual: The figures come from an author-machine capture, not from committed data, and both READMEs say so: "The demo transcript is an illustrative capture from an author's `web` profile (revision unrecorded) — its figures are not reproducible from this repo and drift as the profile gains plugins; the committed fixtures and their pinned outputs live in `fixtures/` and `tests/golden.spec.js`." The transcript itself is captioned the same way in the draft: "以下输出是作者本机 profile 的示意 capture(未记录 harness revision,数字未随仓库提供)", and demo.svg's <desc> adds: "The figures are not reproducible from this repository's synthetic fixtures … The capture records no harness revision or date." A command cannot recompute them. The caption-quoted `~184 tokens` entry ruler is part of the same capture; the fixture-backed cost figures are checked by `hero-ledger-figures`.
